    Google Ads AI Max Is Making More Decisions For You – 6 Settings To Audit Now via @sejournal, @brookeosmundson

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1707 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google Ads is moving more existing Search campaign functionality into AI Max, giving its automation a larger role in how ads are matched, written, and delivered.
    • Recent findings suggest that campaigns using automatically created assets and campaign-level broad match settings already began transitioning in September 2026.
    • Google claims the automatic upgrades are designed to preserve existing campaign settings.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google Ads is moving more existing Search campaign functionality into AI Max, giving its automation a larger role in how ads are matched, written, and delivered.

    Recent findings suggest that campaigns using automatically created assets and campaign-level broad match settings already began transitioning in September 2026. Dynamic Search Ads will follow in February 2027.

    Google claims the automatic upgrades are designed to preserve existing campaign settings. However, AI Max also brings additional controls and optimization options that advertisers have the option to enable.

    For PPC managers, this is a good time to review which decisions Google is already making, which settings are active in your accounts, and whether those settings are aligned with your business goals.

    Here’s what to audit before giving AI Max more control over existing Search campaigns.

    Before changing anything, it’s crucial to understand how AI Max is currently configured across your accounts, if at all.

    In a recent development, google’s migration process doesn’t enable every AI Max feature automatically for every campaign. The settings depend on which legacy functionality each campaign was using.

    According to Google’s migration documentation:.

    This is why it’s worth checking each campaign, because two campaigns showing AI Max as enabled may have very different levels of automation running.

    According to recent reports, within Google Ads, review the AI Max settings at both the campaign and ad group levels. Specifically, check whether search term matching, text customization, and Final URL expansion are active.

    Search term matching can be controlled at the ad group level, while text customization and Final URL expansion are campaign-level settings.

    I’d also look at whether any campaigns have different configurations than expected, especially those that were recently migrated or created using Google’s default settings.

    According to recent reports, the goal here is to establish what’s running before making additional changes. Otherwise, it becomes difficult to evaluate which AI Max features are influencing performance.

    Search term matching is one of the areas I’d spend the most time reviewing, especially in campaigns with tightly defined keyword strategies.

    AI Max can use broad match and keywordless matching technology to identify additional searches based on existing keywords, ads, and landing pages.

    While it can help campaigns reach relevant searches that weren’t covered by the original keyword list, it’s also notorious for introducing traffic that doesn’t fit the campaign’s intended purpose.

    Research from Mike Ryan at Smarter Ecommerce (SMEC) demonstrates how much AI Max can expand beyond an advertiser’s existing keyword targeting.

    In an analysis of 383 million impressions, Ryan found that more than 25% of impressions attributed to exact match keywords in AI Max-enabled Search campaigns came through AI Max search term matching.

    That doesn’t mean those searches were necessarily irrelevant. However, it does show why advertisers shouldn’t assume exact match keywords are limiting traffic to their original targeting.

    Google’s AI Max reporting documentation outlines additional reporting fields that can help advertisers understand how searches are being matched.

    When reviewing Search terms, I’d focus on:.

    Competitor searches might deserve some extra attention, based on Ryan’s research.

    In SMEC’s research, Ryan documented one account where competitor searches accounted for 69% of total Search impressions.

    That’s a single-account example, but it reveals how heavily the traffic mix can lean toward searches outside the advertiser’s original targeting.

    I also wouldn’t judge every newly introduced search term solely by whether it converts immediately.

    Some campaigns may have some wiggle room to support earlier-stage research, especially when there’s enough budget to fund it without taking away from stronger existing demand.

    However, if a campaign is already struggling to capture its highest-intent searches, expanding into more informational traffic might be worth excluding for the time being.

    Negative keywords remain available with AI Max, along with brand controls and ad group-level locations of interest.

    Text customization allows Google to generate additional headlines and descriptions using existing ads, keywords, and landing page content.

    For advertisers already using automatically created assets, the audit should focus on what’s being generated and how those assets are performing.

    Google’s optimized asset reporting provides additional performance metrics, including spend and conversions, to help advertisers evaluate the assets being served.

    I’d look closely at three areas:.

    A generated headline could be technically accurate for the business but inappropriate for the campaign’s audience.

    This deserves additional review in industries with legal, compliance, or partner messaging requirements.

    Google allows advertisers to review and remove generated assets. It has also introduced AI Brief and text disclaimer controls to provide additional guidance over generated messaging.

    See also: Should You Use Auto-Generated Creative? – Ask A PPC.

    There’s another consideration for campaigns that rely on responsive search ad pinning.

    Google’s AI Max documentation confirms that pinning isn’t always respected when Final URL expansion is enabled.

    Recent findings suggest that when Google selects a different landing page, it may generate ad copy that better matches that destination rather than using the advertiser’s pinned assets. Pinning also isn’t respected when URL inclusions are provided.

    For campaigns with required disclaimers, pricing language, or partner-approved messaging, I’d check whether the current settings support those requirements.

    If pinning is essential, Google recommends avoiding Final URL expansion and URL inclusions.

    When Final URL expansion is enabled, Google can select a different landing page from the advertiser’s website based on the search query.

    That may help when a website has several relevant product or service pages, but it can also create problems when the destination doesn’t align with the campaign’s goals.

    A website might contain informational articles, support documentation, and pages promoting services outside the campaign’s intended focus.

    Those pages could be relevant to someone’s search, but not something worth spending PPC dollars on.

    Google’s landing page and search term reporting can help identify which URLs are receiving traffic through AI Max.

    For lead generation, I’d also look beyond the initial form submission.

    Recent findings suggest that A landing page might generate more leads while attracting more unqualified customers. That can be difficult to identify without qualified lead or sales data.

    Google supports URL exclusions at the campaign level and URL inclusions at the ad group level.

    Those controls can help advertisers limit where traffic goes without necessarily turning off Final URL expansion across an entire campaign.

    For accounts with tightly controlled conversion experiences, I’d review the available URLs before enabling broader expansion.

    See also: Should Your PPC Strategy Focus On The Lead Pipeline Or Revenue?

    Google has reported that advertisers using the full AI Max feature suite see an average of 7% more conversions or conversion value at a similar CPA or ROAS compared with using search term matching alone.

    That figure comes from Google’s internal 2026 data for non-retail advertisers, and it shouldn’t be treated as an expected result for every account.

    Independent research from Smarter Ecommerce offers another perspective.

    In a March 2026 analysis of more than 250 campaigns, Mike Ryan found that AI Max generated a median 13% more conversion value relative to the remaining campaign revenue.

    However, those conversions came at a median CPA that was 16% higher than the campaign baseline.

    ROAS results also varied considerably. While the median difference was 0%, individual campaign results ranged from 42% above baseline to 35% below it.

    Recent findings suggest that these figures come from observational campaign data rather than controlled experiments measuring incremental performance. Ryan also noted that the analysis couldn’t account for potential cannibalization across campaigns.

    Sources indicate that the research doesn’t mean AI Max is underperforming across the board. It suggests that additional conversion volume may come at a higher cost, with results varying significantly between accounts.

    Sources indicate that if broader matching is reaching more informational or earlier-stage searches, those people may need more time before converting. Some may never become customers.

    For lead generation, I’d compare the quality of conversions coming through AI Max against existing traffic. Are those leads qualified? Are they turning into opportunities or customers?

    For ecommerce, revenue, ROAS, margin, and the products being sold can provide more information than conversion volume alone.

    Google has expanded its AI Max experimentation tools, including the ability to maintain brand and location controls during testing.

    For campaigns that haven’t fully adopted AI Max, experiments can help compare performance before enabling additional functionality.

    I’d avoid changing several settings at once because it’s more difficult to attribute performance swings to a particular feature set of AI Max.

    It has been revealed that if the goal is to understand whether broader matching improves performance, structure the test around that decision. The same applies to Final URL expansion or text customization.

    Google’s experiment setup has eligibility restrictions, so not every existing campaign can use the same testing approach.

    For campaigns already migrated with legacy functionality enabled, reviewing current performance may help identify which settings are worth testing next.

    Advertisers still running Dynamic Search Ads have time before Google’s automatic migration begins in February 2027.

    Google says the migration will convert dynamic ad groups into standard ad groups while preserving supported legacy settings and data. Its upgrade documentation also notes that unsupported legacy DSA targets may become read-only.

    I’d review existing dynamic ad targets, URL exclusions, and search term performance before the transition.

    Some campaigns may contain targeting decisions that made sense when they were created but haven’t been revisited recently.

    For advertisers with complex websites or large inventories, confirming which pages and services should remain eligible is worth doing before the migration.

    I wouldn’t approach this audit by immediately turning off AI Max features or adding restrictions across every Search campaign.

    Some accounts may benefit from giving Google more flexibility to find relevant searches, customize messaging, and select landing pages.

    I’d start with campaigns where those decisions could have the greatest impact on performance or where existing controls serve a clear purpose.

    That includes campaigns with limited budgets, strict lead qualification requirements, regulated messaging, or carefully managed landing page experiences.

    For campaigns already performing well, reviewing current settings and reporting may be enough to determine whether additional testing is worthwhile.

    Industry observers note that as Google moves more Search functionality into AI Max, advertisers still have control over several crucial decisions. Knowing what’s enabled, how Google is using that flexibility, and what results the business is receiving should guide where those controls are applied.

    All the latest headlines and insights from the world of digital journalism and publishing. Our daily newsletter is a must-read from newsrooms to executive suites.

    We will never sell your address. Prefer a weekly email?

    Nearly there — check your email.

    Recent findings suggest that we have sent a confirmation link to . Click it and you are on the list. If it has not turned up in a minute or two, it may be in your spam folder.

    Vox users can watch videos and listen to podcasts in the app, but reading stories requires a paid subscription.

    Vox has introduced its first mobile application, the publication best known for its explanatory journalism unveiled Wednesday morning.

    Growing membership is a “key priority,” managing editor for audience and membership Bill Carey said. Vox believes launching the app is one way to do that. A Vox membership costs $5 per month, or $60 per year, and offers ad-free versions of podcasts and unlimited access to all of the website’s contents.

    RELATED ARTICLEVox is revamping its editorial strategy to redefine what ‘Voxxy’ meansHanaa' TameezNovember 8, 2021Strengthening its relationship to its audience is only becoming more crucial for Vox. The app launch comes at a time when news publishers are increasingly trying to keep users on their own platforms amid growing preferences for AI summaries, news creators, and industry-wide traffic declines.

    Industry observers note that “The move toward developing our membership program in the last couple of years has really been about understanding how key it is for us to build more community and to foster that loyalty [of our] audience,” Carey stated. “When we were looking at that, it really felt like an app was a good way to continue pointing in that direction.”.

    It has been revealed that vox isn’t the only news outlet focusing on mobile apps. The Verge — Vox’s former sister publication under Vox Media — named traffic declines as one of the reasons why it plans to launch its own app next year. The Wall Street Journal’s head of digital, Taneth Evans, recently stated that the Journal makes its app more useful to customers by offering all of its mediums in one place. Evans also said that news publishers “need to give people reasons to open an app beyond simply offering news.”.

    “Websites will become a service for agents,” Evans noted. “Apps are gonna be the thing that humans will connect with.”.

    Sources indicate that vox declined to provide website traffic numbers, but data from Comscore reveals that the website’s unique visitors decreased by 36% year-over-year between September 2025 (7.4 million) and September 2026 (4.8 million). Archived data from SimilarWeb shows the site had 20.8 million visits in September 2021.

    “Vox isn’t immune to the larger trends that have led to web traffic declines in recent years, but those only represent a portion of our audience,” Carey said in an email. “Vox is focused on building audience engagement across platforms, with social video views up 86% year-over-year and newsletter audience up 14%.”.

    “Even if there wasn’t a decline in search traffic, as everyone has been seeing — and we still get members from search — we want to create that relationship with our audience,” publisher and editor-in-chief Swati Sharma said. “People know Vox and they have a relationship with Vox. We have a younger audience that’s on all of these different platforms. I think it is definitely a part of building that relationship ourselves.”.

    According to recent reports, that the app makes all Vox content accessible in one place for current and future members also signals the “un-siloing” of the newsroom overall, Sharma said. Vox presently has 78 editorial employees.

    Sources indicate that RELATED ARTICLESwati Sharma is leading a newly introduced era in Vox’s mission to “explain the world”Hanaa' TameezMay 6, 2021When Sharma, who has helmed Vox.com since 2021, first arrived, she found that Vox’s main mediums (text, audio, and video) “weren’t in service of one another.” The “silos” allowed teams to build their own audiences and products. But while teams discussed story ideas with each other and during editorial meetings, “they all [needed] to go into their creative spaces and find what works for their medium and not be in service of just one larger section.”.

    That’s changed over the past five years, Sharma stated. Each team — text, video, and audio — does a little bit of everything now. Text reporters appear on podcasts and in videos, while podcasters and hosts also write their own newsletters.

    Recent findings suggest that “In a lot of newsrooms, there’s one dominant form, and at Vox, there wasn’t. They’re all really notable,” Sharma remarked. “[Senior correspondent] Dylan Scott is on our Unexplainable podcast talking about Alzheimer’s. [Host and editorial director] Astead Herndon does a newsletter and a Substack Live every week, and he does a podcast. That’s the future for us, and that’s where our whole newsroom is moving, where those silos are done and you can basically do everything.”.

    Rank Math SEO WordPress Plugin Hit By 16 Vulnerabilities In 2026 via @sejournal, @martinibuster

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (682 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sixteen vulnerabilities have been discovered in the popular Rank Math SEO plugin in 2026, setting a upcoming record for vulnerabilities discovered, more than any other SEO plugin.
    • Rank Math’s 2026 vulnerabilities included potential pathways to website takeover, exposure of protected information, and unauthorized changes to WordPress content and data.
    • Although AI is making vulnerability disclosures more common, other SEO plugins like Yoast SEO did not have anywhere near that many vulnerability discoveries.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sixteen vulnerabilities have been discovered in the popular Rank Math SEO plugin in 2026, setting a upcoming record for vulnerabilities discovered, more than any other SEO plugin.

    Rank Math’s 2026 vulnerabilities included potential pathways to website takeover, exposure of protected information, and unauthorized changes to WordPress content and data. All of these things could also have a negative impact on SEO.

    Although AI is making vulnerability disclosures more common, other SEO plugins like Yoast SEO did not have anywhere near that many vulnerability discoveries. The free version of Yoast SEO was reported by Wordfence to have a total of four vulnerabilities in 2026 and only two were discovered in the paid version.

    The sixteen vulnerabilities share certain concerns in common but arguably the worst of them are:.

    Remote Code Execution (CVSS rated 8.8) Two vulnerabilities with a CVSS severity score of 8.8 were discovered that could enable attackers with Contributor or Author-level access to execute arbitrary code on the server, potentially leading to complete website compromise.

    In a recent development, arbitrary File Upload (7.2) One of the vulnerabilities could potentially lead to a website takeover through malicious file uploads, although this vulnerability required Administrator privileges. CVE-2026-104752: Arbitrary File Upload, requiring Administrator-level access or higher. Disclosed October 8, 2026. CVSS 7.2 (High).

    In a recent development, stored Cross-Site Scripting (7.2) An unauthenticated attacker could potentially execute malicious JavaScript in an Administrator’s browser. Depending on the circumstances, that could lead to privileged actions or account compromise. CVE-2026-66702: Stored Cross-Site Scripting, requiring no authentication. Disclosed July 31, 2026. CVSS 7.2 (High).

    Stored Cross-Site Scripting (7.2) An unauthenticated attacker could potentially execute malicious JavaScript in an Administrator’s browser. Depending on the circumstances, this could enable an attacker to make unauthorized changes to the website or take control of an Administrator’s account. CVE-2026-66702: Stored Cross-Site Scripting, requiring no authentication. Disclosed July 31, 2026. CVSS 7.2 (High).

    These vulnerabilities could allow attackers to access protected content or sensitive website information without the necessary permissions. Unlike vulnerabilities that enable unauthorized changes, these primarily concern exposing information that should remain restricted, although SQL injection could also allow attackers to manipulate website data.

    Recent findings suggest that these vulnerabilities could enable attackers to make unauthorized changes to a WordPress website, including modifying content-related data, changing homepage settings, and deleting SEO information. Some could be exploited without logging in, while others required an account but allowed actions beyond that user level’s permissions.

    Most vulnerabilities were discovered within a relatively short period. Eleven of the 16 vulnerabilities were discovered between August 27 and October 14, 2026. Of those vulnerabilities, late August and early September saw a concentrated cluster of vulnerability discoveries. Eight were reported between August 27 and September 3, within just eight days.

    The disclosures continued into October. Five vulnerabilities were reported in October, including three disclosed on October 8 and the latest on October 27.

    As previously stated, Rank Math’s direct competitor, Yoast SEO, only experienced four vulnerabilities during a year which saw an increase in vulnerability discoveries. The unusually high number of vulnerabilities leads to questions about Rank Math’s coding practices, code review, and quality control.

    The other issue in the sixteen vulnerabilities is that are repeated instances of the same kinds of exploits.

    Missing authorization was the most frequently identified vulnerability category. Seven of the 16 entries explicitly mention inadequate permission checks, pointing to recurring problems with enforcing permissions before allowing actions.

    Sources indicate that some security problems could lead to complete website compromise. Two vulnerabilities carried CVSS scores of 8.8 and involved remote code execution, allowing attackers who met the required conditions to potentially execute malicious code on the server.

    Overall, the vulnerabilities involved a broad range of security weaknesses. They included unauthorized modifications, information exposure, cross-site scripting, SQL injection, arbitrary file uploads, and remote code execution. The vulnerability discoveries do not point to just one type of coding lapse; they point to a wide range of coding problems.

    The full list of Rank Math vulnerabilities can be found at Wordfence, with links to a description page for each vulnerability.

    Recent findings suggest that curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale.

    We are looking for a Product Builder to join the IDP & RPA pod. You will take real problems from customers, decide what is worth solving, and build and ship the solution yourself, using AI tools to get from idea to production promptly without lowering the bar.

    Product Building is how Camunda's Experience organization builds the applications people use on top of Camunda 8, such as Hub, Operate, and ProcessOS. Small pods of builders own a product area from customer problem to shipped change, with no hand-offs between product management, design, and engineering. We are setting this model up now, so you will help shape how it works.

    According to recent reports, the IDP & RPA pod builds how Camunda processes work with documents and legacy applications. With intelligent document processing (IDP), customers create extraction and classification templates in Camunda Hub and publish them so a process can use AI to turn invoices and other documents into structured data. With robotic process automation (RPA), customers integrate legacy applications that have no APIs, using Robot Framework scripts on a standalone RPA worker. The hard problems come with putting LLMs into customer processes: extraction quality, model and prompt choices, testing and trust, and working for AI agents as well as for people.

    Help shape product direction for IDP & RPA by combining customer input, usage data, and field feedback into clear priorities.

    Partner with the other builders and product strategy to turn problems into shipped features, using short written proposals and prototypes to align early.

    Make judgment calls with incomplete information within your scope and own the outcome.

    Communicate trade-offs and decisions clearly to stakeholders who don't live in the details the way you do.

    Use AI tools across the whole loop, from specs to prototypes to production-ready code, and hold a high bar for what you ship by reviewing and improving the output rather than accepting it.

    Build, test, and ship improvements to the IDP & RPA experience, reading errors and tracing issues far enough to give your pod useful context.

    Talk to customers and to support and customer success colleagues about how IDP is used and where it breaks, and turn what you learn into decisions about what to build next.

    Pick up customer incidents and trace them across Hub, the connectors, and the deployed process of the customer.

    Track what you ship against real outcomes and adjust when the data tells you to.
